t: Appropriations and funds made available and authority granted pursuant to this joint resolution shall remain available until (a) enactment into law of an appropriation for any project or activity provided for in this joint resolution, or (b) enactment of the applicable appropriation Act by both Houses without any provision for such project or activity, or (c) August 31, 1967, whichever first occurs.

fable.w: This section only sets how long continuing-resolution appropriations and authority remain available. The tempting reading is that the reference to action "by both Houses" signals a participatory process, but Congress is inside the federal government and enacting appropriations is ordinary legislation. No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public is consulted, heard or given a right to sue.
fable.s: enactment of the applicable appropriation Act by both Houses without any provision for such project or activity

qwen_block.w: This section defines the expiration date for the availability of federal funds and authority. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or private entities) in the decision-making process. It is purely an internal administrative provision regarding budget authority.
qwen_block.s: Appropriations and funds made available and authority granted pursuant to this joint resolution shall remain available until (a) enactment into law of an appropriation for any project or activity provided for in this joint resolution, or (b) enactment of the applicable appropriation Act by both Houses without any provision for such project or activity, or (c) August 31, 1967, whichever first occurs.

opus.w: This provision only says how long appropriations under a continuing resolution stay available. The only actors are the Houses of Congress, which are inside the federal government. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue.
opus.s: enactment of the applicable appropriation Act by both Houses without any provision for such project or activity

qwen_chat.w: This section solely defines the expiration date for the availability of appropriated funds. It does not establish any mechanism for consultation, coordination, or participation with entities outside the federal government. The only actors mentioned are the legislative bodies (Congress) involved in enacting appropriation acts, which are inside the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: Appropriations and funds made available and authority granted pursuant to this joint resolution shall remain available until (a) enactment into law of an appropriation for any project or activity provided for in this joint resolution, or (b) enactment of the applicable appropriation Act by both Houses without any provision for such project or activity, or (c) August 31, 1967, whichever first occurs.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the funds are for projects, there is an implicit process involving outside parties. However, the text itself only describes the duration of funding availability and conditions related to congressional enactment. It contains no language regarding consultation, hearings, advisory boards, or public comment.
